messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV cache eviction rate spike detected for shard-group eu-1. Pager triggered (P1). avg_kv_evictions/sec increased 12x in last 3m. Affected: continuous-batching hotpath.

lina: paging — i'm oncall. seeing a lot of 5xx traces and backlog growth on the continuous-batcher. linking dashboard: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/kv-evict-eu1

ken: on it. initial hypothesis: a change in gc/eviction heuristics + sudden traffic spike from customers with long contexts. eviction churn blowing out KV size, causing many cache misses and extra compute per-token -> latency + cost spike.

maya: confirmed. 95p latency for text-generation up from 120ms -> 1.8s on eu-1. throughput per-GPU down ~30%. KV cache hit-rate dropped 28%.

lina: impact: some hosted customers seeing failed streaming sessions and elevated cost. Support ticket queue has alerts for two customers (acme-inc, beta-co). raised high-sev notes to account teams. eva, can you surface top 5 tenants by error rate?

eva: acme-inc (errors 4.5%), beta-co (errors 2.1%), dev-ops-play (1.6%), internal-test (1.2%), demo-corp (0.9%).

ken: mitigation options: 1) global reduce continuous_batching.window_ms and disable aggressive prefix caching for a short period. 2) per-tenant override to force `continuous_batching.enabled=false` for impacted customers. 3) emergency canary rollback of the recent kv-eviction heuristic change (but that's a risky code rollback). prefer 1+2 to keep infra changes minimal.

lina: agree prioritize feature-flag based mitigations. we should do per-customer overrides for acme-inc and beta-co then a global softening if still unhealthy.

maya: prepping commands. will canary per-tenant override first for acme-inc. will route 100% traffic for acme-inc to non-batched path (instant effect).

ken: also add a short-lived global flag: `batching.window_ms=20` (was 50) and `batching.max_batch=8` (was 64). That will reduce memory pressure and KV churn. we need to watch latency tail.

lina: outline live roll steps:
1) per-tenant override for acme-inc -> monitor 2m
2) per-tenant override for beta-co -> monitor 2m
3) if still high eviction rates, flip global softening flags -> monitor 5m
4) if stable, promote global flags as short lived mitigation and open rollback PR for the heuristic.

ken: executing per-tenant override for acme-inc now:
```bash
# feature-flag service
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/api/v1/overrides \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FLAG_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-inc","overrides":{"continuous_batching.enabled":false}}'
```

lina: eva, mark support and sales that acme-inc traffic is being forced to non-batched path.

eva: noted, pinged acme-team slack and opened sync with AM.

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted: override for acme-inc queued to flags-service (req_id=ff-9876).

maya: override applied. seeing immediate drop in eviction rate for shards serving acme-inc. overall eviction rate down ~6x.

lina: good. monitor 2m and then roll beta-co.

ken: applying beta-co override now. same curl with tenant=beta-co.

deploy-bot: deploy accepted (req_id=ff-9877).

maya: applied. after both overrides, global eviction rate down 8x from peak. 95p latency improved to ~380ms. streaming failures for acme-inc/beta-co dropped to baseline.

lina: excellent. next step: consider global softening. ken, are you comfortable toggling batching.window_ms and batching.max_batch?

ken: yes. plan: update runtime flag service and push to canary pool (10% of host machines) first, monitor with dashboards and profiler. command: 
```bash
# set short lived runtime flags
rtctl set global batching.window_ms=20 batching.max_batch=8 --ttl=60m --canary=10%
```

maya: applying canary now to 10% of runtime nodes.

deploy-bot: runtime flag change accepted (req_id=rt-3344).

maya: canary looks healthy on canary nodes. eviction rate on canary slices down, no spike in tail latency beyond expected. promoting to 50% next.

lina: promote when you see stable metrics for 3 consecutive 1m intervals.

maya: promoting to 50%.

ken: promoting to 100% now. global eviction rate back to baseline, 95p latency at ~210ms. CPU usage on GPUs normalized.

lina: leaving per-tenant overrides in place for acme-inc and beta-co for now while we validate customer-facing sessions. eva, keep AMs updated and patch support notes with mitigation steps.

eva: will do. I updated ticket and alerted acme-inc slack. they acknowledged and said errors stopped for them.

ken: root cause triage notes: a recent change in eviction scoring (+0.15 aggressiveness) combined with a burst of long-context requests increased cache churn. continuous-batching kept trying to merge prefixes which led to larger KV foot prints and page churn. We'll revert or tune eviction scoring in next patch.

lina: actions/todo:
- (ken) open rollback PR for kv-eviction heuristic and run perf tests (P0)
- (maya) run longer 6h soak on canary flags and capture traffic slices (P1)
- (eva) coordinate customer comms and close support tickets after 1h stable (P1)
- (lina) write incident note and schedule postmortem (P1)

ken: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/kv/changes/PR-4321 (wip). will include option to bound eviction delta by tenant memory profile.

maya: metrics to capture for postmortem: per-tenant KV size, eviction/sec, continuous-batch average batch size, 95/99 latency, streaming failure rate.

lina: good. setting bridge to postmortem channel and capturing logs.

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged, bridge created: https://incidents.redwood/bridge/IN-2026-kv-evict

lina: summary for timeline:
- 00:00 alert triggered by eviction spike -> pager (incident-bot)
- 00:02 per-tenant overrides for acme-inc and beta-co applied
- 00:06 global batching softening canary -> promoted -> 00:12 global flags at 100%
- 00:20 eviction rates normalized, errors reduced for impacted customers

dan: quick note on costs: we saw a 3x token compute bill on eu-1 during the peak. finance will want a short report.

lina: noted. add to postmortem.

maya: we'll leave per-tenant overrides in place for 2h then roll-down if stable. I'll monitor and report back here.

ken: if anyone sees eviction rate climb again, immediate action = reapply per-tenant override + roll global flags back to conservative values.

lina: thanks all. holding here for 30m to confirm stability. keep chatter in this thread for the postmortem log.

maya: 00:40 follow-up: after 30m stable, starting to remove override for dev-test tenants (internal-test, dev-ops-play) and observing no regressions. keeping acme-inc and beta-co for 2h.

lina: closing pager for now but keeping incident open. will post final incident summary when PR and follow-up actions are done. :white_check_mark:
